author: Jason Fanelli
description:
At this year's New York Comic Con, I met with Square Enix to check out two of its upcoming RPG projects. One was Final Fantasy VII Revelation, a game firmly planted in the modern era of video games with top-of-the-line visuals and all the trimmings of a AAA, big-budget game. 

The other was Romancing Saga 3: Destinies United, a remake of a classic turn-based RPG from the mid-1990s. At first glance, the remake's updated visuals and faster gameplay are easily apparent draws for newer players, but that doesn't change that this game is built around the core of the original Romancing Saga 3, an RPG that calls back to a bygone era for the genre. Remaking a classic like this is a balancing act, but based on my brief time playing the game, it seems like Square Enix is on track to unite
title: A Sentient Snowman Is (Surprisingly) My Favorite Part Of This RPG Remake

author: Alessandro Barbosa
description:
Thanks to devices such as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, as well as the ongoing issues with Windows, gaming on Linux looks a lot more attractive over the last few years. Its biggest hurdle is still multiplayer games and their anti-cheat systems, but Epic Games is committed to bringing one of the biggest around to the operating system soon.

Epic Games has announced that it is working on a Linux version for Fortnite. It's going to act as a test for Epic's overhaul of EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat), its solution to those developing multiplayer games in Unreal Engine to prevent cheating (most recently used in Gears of War: E-Day). Epic says that it has offered Linux support for its current version of EAC, but that most developers (it
title: Epic Is Overhauling Its Anti-Cheat So That Fortnite Can Finally Come To A New Platform

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Microsoft is reportedly surveying a subset of Xbox users about changing its plans for exclusive games going forward--possibly in a big way--and that's no surprise given Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has alluded to changes to the exclusivity strategy in the future.

At the same time, a survey like this is not necessarily indicative of anything beyond Microsoft conducting research. After all, there is an entire team at Xbox called Xbox Research that ... researches all manner of things, and the results of that research d
title: Xbox Survey About Exclusives Includes A Nuclear Strategy, But Wait Just A Minute

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 releases on November 19, but when will you be able to read reviews? According to historical precedent and a new report, reviews for the open-world crime game should be available before launch.

Insider Gaming reported that reviews for GTA 6 will be posted at some point before November 19, but the exact timing is unknown for now. According to insider
title: GTA 6 Reviews: When They Could Be Released

author: Ben Janca
description: From classic arcade games to LEGO Marvel and Marvel Snap, Vision has been part of gaming history for decades. We're breaking down his biggest video game appearances ahead of Marvel's VisionQuest.
title: The History of Vision in Marvel Video Games

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave has some of the best tactical gameplay in the series to date, but actually digging into the art of seeing units bonk each other on the head in turn-based combat is a massive slog. Between a shift to Persona-like storytelling and a laundry list of chores, the game can feel like the equivalent of the Achilles and the tortoise paradox (via a Jujutsu Kaisen breakdown), because the closer I get to actually moving the story forward, the further I feel I am from actually engaging in some of that fantastic warfare.

And that's a shame, because Fortune's Weave is a really great evolution of the core Fire Emblem gameplay experience. The tactics game has more nuance to its rock-paper-nuns-wit
title: I’m Enjoying Fire Emblem More By Not Playing Fire Emblem More

author: Levi Winslow
description:
The Electronic Software Association (ESA) has a serious bone to pick with retro handhelds that are packaged with tons of unlicensed pre-installed, calling these devices "superfakes" that should face some sort of suppression by the US government.

According to an October 6 filing with the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR)--which monitors marketplaces that are accused of engaging in or enabling piracy and counterfeiting--the ESA is urging the government to clamp down on what it calls "illicit plug-and-play consoles and handheld devices." The ESA wants the USTR to add these emulation devices to the Notorious Markets List, the agency's annual report identifying which markets are participating in such behavior, thereby barring or slowing their profits.

"In the video game sector, illicit plug-and-pl
title: Retro Handhelds Loaded With Unlicensed Games Could Face Government Crackdown

author: Cameron Koch
description:
World of Warcraft: Forever isn't out yet, but it's already clear it has a major problem. It isn't anything in the game itself. It's not the addition of Skyborne elves that require players to pay $30, or controversial class changes like Warrior's Rage normalization. The WoW Classic community is a passionate bunch, and so there's a huge variety of strong opinions on everything related to the latest version of developer Blizzard's old-school MMORPG. That's all par for the course. Instead, it's a problem that's largely out of the community's control: streamers.

Streamers have been a big part of WoW since Twitch's earliest days. The release of WoW Classic back in 2019 in particular was a watershed moment, with 1.1 million concurrent viewers and 55 million hours w
title: WoW: Forever Has A Streamer Problem

author: Jordan Ramée
description:
Originally slated for this year, At Fate's End has been delayed to 2027. And while I'm bummed that the next game from Spiritfarer studio Thunder Lotus is now months (maybe even a year) away, the new Steam demo that dropped alongside the delay announcement has been an excellent consolation prize. Having finished the one-hour slice of the upcoming action-adventure, I'm more convinced than ever that this game would have been a serious contender for everyone's Best Of lists this year had it managed to stick to its original release window. 

Like Spiritfarer, At Fate's End appears to combine an engrossing gameplay loop with an emotionally devastating story. However, unlike Spiritfarer, At Fate's End isn't delving into
title: My Most-Anticipated Game Was Delayed, But Its New Demo Has Proven A Fantastic Consolation

author: Jessica Cogswell
description:
Being the face of a video game is a demanding role, as the people who step into these positions involved in these roles often find themselves on the receiving end of a lot of toxicity. Former Overwatch game director Jeff Kaplan knows this all too well, as he promoted the hero shooter for several years and regularly interacted with its fans--albeit at a "personal cost." 

After leaving Blizzard Entertainment in 2021, Kaplan has been quietly working on The Legend of California, the in-development game at his new
title: Ex-Overwatch Director Jeff Kaplan Says He Never Wanted The Spotlight, But The Game Needed A Face

author: Cameron Koch
description:
Jeff Kaplan, Overwatch's former director, said he's not played the game he was the public face of since April 2021, when he left developer Blizzard after nearly 20 years to go indie. He called his relationship with Blizzard's shooter one of "clinical separation."

Kaplan revealed this to GameSpot in an interview that dove into his history with Blizzard and the creation of his new game, The Legend of California. 

When asked if he had continu
title: Jeff Kaplan Says Seperation From Overwatch Was “Clinical”: ” I Never Go Back”

author: Jessica Cogswell
description:
"Have you ever seen Napoleon Dynamite?"

I'll admit it: When I sat down with former Blizzard developer Jeff Kaplan to discuss his legacy and what comes next, I hadn't anticipated being asked questions myself--especially ones pertaining to one of the early aughts' most iconic (and absurd) comedy films. Yet it took only 20 minutes until we reached this point--when discussing the tragedy of Uncle Rico felt like a both a natural and important conversation to have.

Despite being a self-proclaimed introvert, it's easy to see how the World of Warcraft developer went on to become not just the director of Overwatch, but the highly public face of the game. There is an openness to Kaplan that fosters trust--a warmth that makes conversation feel natural. This quality was most assuredly what Blizzard was looking for as it readied itself to launch a new tentpole title that needed to make World of
title: Jeff Kaplan Was An Industry Icon, Now Peers Ignore His Emails: Ex-Overwatch Director Talks “Humbling” Reality Of Indie Dev

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Google has released its list of the "top trending costumes" ahead of Halloween, and Minecraft's Verity has made the cut.

The Frightgeist list, as it's called, is based on what's trending on Google. The list is topped by Buddy the Unicorn from director Casper Kelly's horror movie. The character Nikki from Curry Barker's viral horror hit Obsession makes the cut, too.

Verity ranks No. 7. For anyone just catching up, Verity is a horror web series from ThatMob, and it takes place inside Minecraft. The character Verity is a smiling face that becomes increasingly unhinged--you can watch the full movie below. This is not to be co
title: Minecraft’s Verity Is A Top Trending Halloween Costume For 2026

author: Jason Fanelli
description:
Since the release of the first game of the trilogy in 2020, I have been heavily invested in the Final Fantasy 7 Remake saga. 

I've spent over 100 hours between the first two games, Remake and Rebirth, entrenching myself in this remade version of Gaia, re-acquainting myself with Cloud and the gang, and peeling back layer after layer of this reimagined story. Revelation, the upcoming third installment, is a finale 11 years in the making (if you start counting from FF7 Remake's initial E3 2015 reveal trailer), and I went into the latest demo for Revelation ready to learn more about this final chapter. 

After playing through Revelation's opening 25 minutes, however, I'm left not with answers, but more questions.
title: FF7 Revelation’s Opening Invites Deeply Intriguing Questions About The Trilogy’s Conclusion

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Microsoft has announced a new controlled called the Xbox Nano Controller, and it's smaller than the existing Xbox controller, and it costs less.

Microsoft says the controller is designed to fit nearly every pocket and budget. "Its compact design offers a great option for younger players, smaller hands, or anyone seeking something portable for play on the go," the company said.
title: Xbox Nano Controller Announced, And It’s So Small

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
PlayStation has revealed this month's batch of new arrivals for the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog. Most of these games will be available starting October 20.

Don’t forget, all PS Plus members can claim three freebies this month–F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896, and Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2–but you only have until November 2 to do so.

Kicking things off in October is Mafia: The Old Country, a prequel to the original trilogy of Mafia games. If you're looking for something that won't take you too long to play, has a great story, and solid action gameplay, it's a great option f
title: PlayStation Plus Extra/Premium Games For October 2026 Revealed

author: Callum Self
description:
Since Phantom Blade Zero’s reveal back in… 2023?! Really? Wow, it’s been that long. Since its reveal, the action RPG has been stuck in my brain like a dream I can’t quite escape. Its fast-paced combat, which delicately combines offense and defense, looks like a dance of death, as gripping as it is dangerous. I’m ready to dive into the Phantom World, and if you are, too, you may as well save some money with a pre-order discount.

My excitement has only grown with the recent wave of previews ahead of the game’s release. The promise of intense, satisfying action in GameSpot’s Phantom Blade Zero preview from Max Blumenthal only made me more excited for the upcoming game. Wh
title: Tango Into The Dance Of Death With Phantom Blade Zero At A Pre-Order Discount

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Ubisoft has announced that it plans to shut down Trials developer RedLynx as part of its ongoing restructuring efforts, as well as reduce the workforce of its Skull and Bones studio, Ubisoft Singapore, by laying off 72 people. The closure of the Finland-based RedLynx is in a proposal stage, and Ubisoft says that because the studio isn't currently working on a new project, it makes more economic sense to close it down and retrench its 52 employees instead.

Under Finnish law (via Kotaku), Ubisoft is legally required to consult and negotiate with employees before it makes major changes to the studio, which is why Ubisoft hasn't officially announced yet that it will shut down RedLynx--although it's likely only a matter of time. The studio was first formed in 2000, and it's best known fo
title: Ubisoft’s Latest Restructuring Plan Puts Trials Developer RedLynx On The Chopping Block

author: Eddie Makuch
description: Rockstar Games has reacted to the mass GTA 6 leaks, which began in 2022, with a top developer at the studio saying it "feels like somebody's wading through your dirty washing."
title: GTA 6 Leaks Are Still Coming, Rockstar Labels The 2022 Hack “Weirdly Invasive”

author: Eddie Makuch
description: A big new report revealed more details about Rockstar's long-awaited GTA 6, including how the game's scope was originally much bigger and that the game could have released years sooner.
title: GTA 6 Could Have Been Even Bigger And Released Years Sooner, But Then These Things Happened

author: Steve Watts
description:
The young adventurer Link has been entrusted with an epic quest that will take him to every corner of the globe. He is fated to do incredible things, to become the Hero of Time, but for now he is just a boy. He says farewell to his dearest friend, Saria, and, with his trusty sword and his fairy Navi in tow, he steps out of his tiny community of forest children and finds himself in awe of the wider world. As he gazes out, he realizes this vast untamed wilderness is … maybe the size of a couple of football fields? Thereabouts?

I was there when Ocarina of Time first released in 1998, and like many young gamers, my mind was blown. This was one of our earliest experiences with 3D exploration in an open world, and it truly felt vast. The central hub of Hyrule Field was large enough to gracefully cross on horseback. Almost 30 years later, though, the once-majestic Hyrule Field lacks its original luster.
title: Hyrule Field Sure Feels Empty In Ocarina Of Time These Days

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake looks to be a mostly faithful modernization of the classic game, with a few quality-of-life tweaks and updated visuals to make it play like a modern game. One of the more controversial of these is the addition of a jump button, which the original game famously lacked. But now having gotten hands-on with the remake, I can say that the addition of a jump is a good change, and Ocarina is better for it. 

Ocarina was designed without a jump button, and to be clear, the addition of one doesn't transform this into a platformer. Based on my limited experience, the need to jump is occasional and often simple, just clearing small gaps. This geometry was never created to ask you to handle complex jumping challenges and the remake doesn't appear to have any intention
title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake’s Dedicated Jump Button Is Good, Actually

author: Steve Watts
description: The remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is primed to be the crown jewel of this year's Nintendo lineup--after all, this is a lovely-looking reimagining of a beloved and classic entry in one of the most revered video game franchises in the company's catalogue. Ocarina has received the remake treatment before for the 3DS handheld, but that left many of the core systems and the graphical art direction of the original Nintendo 64 game largely intact, albeit cleaner. This Switch 2 remake, by comparison, appears to be making more ambitious changes, while still carefully retaining the original's core identity. Check out our full Ocarina of Time preview for more details, but for a quick primer, here are the six biggest ways that this remake is transforming the experience of the original game.
title: 6 Biggest Takeaways From Hands-On With Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
After publishing his review of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, Hideo Kojima-who says his body is 70% made of movies--has posted his review of one of the most divisive mainstream films of the year. Yes, we're talking about Alejandro Iñárritu's satirical black comedy Digger, which stars Tom Cruise.

Kojima said Digger is a "film that all of us living in today's world should see."

He added: "It is a work that remains with the audience, provoking reflection and sounding alarms."

Kojima doesn't get
title: Hideo Kojima Reviews 2026’s Most Divisive Movie, Digger

author: Steve Watts
description:
Did The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time need another remake? Ocarina is an all-time classic, but it's rooted in a particular time and place in gaming history. How would the new Ocarina of Time balance respect for its original design with modernization? Would it feel like old angular game geometry with an updated paintjob, or would it stray so far from its original design that it no longer feels like Ocarina at all? All of this was on my mind as I sat to play a lengthy portion at a demo event.

I'm pleased to report that Ocarina of Time is still a masterpiece, and more importantly, this remake appears to largely strike the right balance of reverence and renovation to make it feel modern without losing its original charm.

My demo consisted of three sections: young Link's start in Kokiri Forest and some adventuring inside the Deku Tree; young Link leaving the forest and exploring Hyr
title: My Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Skepticism Vanished After Playing It

author: Max Blumenthal
description: I was skeptical that Ocarina needed another remake, but gorgeous visuals, modernized controls, and quality-of-life features help this classic shine brightly again.
title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Has Figured Out How To Balance Old With New | Preview

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description: Developer miHoYo has made a name for itself with its various anime-inspired live-service games, but for its next project, it's taking a page out of the Elden Ring and Monster Hunter playbooks with a dark fantasy adventure called Nodusfall. There's a whole lot that we don't know about the game just yet, but following its official reveal at the 2026 edition of Gamescom Opening Night Live, a few details have trickled out regarding the multiplayer fantasy title. Ahead of its eventual release, here's everything that we know about it, so far.
title: Nodusfall – Gameplay, Beta Dates, And Everything We Know So Far

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally coming out on November 19, but the game was originally set to release in 2025. When the development team informed head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, that a delay to May 2026 was necessary, she made a call to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick to let him know. Months later, she had to make that call again, informing Zelnick that a second delay to November 2026 was required to deliver Rockstar's full ambition for GTA 6.

His response? “I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” Kolbe told
title: Take-Two CEO’s Response To Second GTA 6 Delay: “Please Tell Me You’re Kidding”

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
How much detail is too much detail? In the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar Games put an obscene amount of work into making the fictional city of Leonida as realistic as possible, including the nightclubs that players can frequent in the game. Those locations couldn't be pulled from thin air, and Rockstar embarked on several research trips to Miami to help inform the design of their party hubs, right down to the smallest detail.

Speaking to Bloomberg, artist Aaron Garbut revealed that the developers embarked on ridealongs with police officers, visited trendy nightclubs, and mingled with dancers at these establishments. The result of these excursions was that the Rockstar team could draw on a wealth of knowledge to create authentic hangout spots, with these lo
title: GTA 6’s Nightclubs Have An Absurd Amount Of Detail, Right Down To The Lighting

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
It's no secret that video game development is more expensive than ever before, and in a hit-driven industry, Grand Theft Auto VI is rumored to be the most expensive game ever made. Various numbers have been thrown around, with one report even claiming that $1.5 billion was spent--around the budget of Dubai's iconic Burj Khalifa skyscraper.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Rockstar shot down that claim, but it hasn't confirmed just how much investment it has taken to get the game over the finish line for its November release. With years of development behind it, multiple s
title: Rockstar Says GTA 6 Didn’t Cost $1.5 Billion To Make, But Won’t Reveal The Real Number

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Rockstar Games reportedly established an entire studio in Los Angeles dedicated to creating NPCs for Grand Theft Auto 6 after realizing the game's ambitious world would need far more production resources than initially expected.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Rockstar development lead Rob Nelson explained that the team had struggled to meet its targets for the number of NPCs that needed to be written and animated. That makes sense when you consider how much more interactive they're reported to be, even noticing and reacting when you're carrying a weapon. The numbers were so concerning that they were a large reason for the first GTA 6 dela
title: Rockstar Built An Entire Studio Just To Create GTA 6 NPCs

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Compared to previous games in the series, Grand Theft Auto 6 is aiming to add new layers of realism to the franchise. As the criminal couple Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, players will explore a city where actions have consequences, and it's not easy to shake the long arm of the law when you cause chaos. It continues ideas that developer Rockstar Games began experimenting with in Red Dead Redemption 2, but the studio says it initially struggled to figure out how realistic it wanted GTA 6 to be while still offering a fun gameplay experience.

As detailed by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, Rockstar had a foundation to build on for GTA 6, as it would once again be a sat
title: Rockstar’s GTA 6 Realism Experiment Started With Beer And Sandwiches

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Vibe-coded games playable in web browsers have exploded in popularity recently, and amid a deluge of ports and remasters created with generative AI, Xbox is responding by creating Xbox Labs. The new branch of Xbox is described as an initiative designed to get more people playing games--especially on web browsers--but curiously, there's no mention of AI at all in the announcement.

"In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote. "Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of an
title: Xbox Is Getting Into AI Gaming, Even If It Won’t Say So

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Rockstar has spent more than eight years developing Grand Theft Auto 6, but the studio hopes its next project will arrive considerably faster. Speaking to Bloomberg, Rockstar's head of development Phil Hooker explained how the company expanded its team and developed its technology for the hotly anticipated upcoming game, and how that'll make it easier to build future releases.

Hooker said the studio expects to benefit from the foundations established during the lengthy production of GTA 6. "The engine, the tools, and the team we've built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly," he explained.
title: Rockstar Says You Won’t Have To Wait Another 8 Years After GTA 6 For Its Next Game

author: Kevin Knezevic
description:
Pokemon Go is celebrating the changing of the seasons with a Fall Marathon, and as part of the event, a ghostly new Pokemon has arrived in time for Halloween. The haunted tumbleweed Bramblin is now appearing for a limited time, making this your first chance to catch one in the mobile game, but tracking one down may not be so straightforward.

Unlike most of the event's other featured Pokemon, Bramblin will only appear under certain circumstances, so you'll need to put in a bit of work if you're hoping to add one to your collection. To help out, here are some tips on how to catch and evolve Bramblin before the Fall Marathon event ends.
title: How To Get Bramblin In Pokemon Go
